Let the catalog sell and the voice order: A storefront that suggests items earns its keep on a buyer who is browsing with time to spare. The reorder at the end of a shift is not that moment. The two jobs can sit together without arguing.
Same account, two different moments: A chef might click through a catalog on a quiet Tuesday and speak the Friday order standing in the walk-in. Nobody has to pick one way of ordering for good.
Orders land where they already land: Whatever you add, the order still arrives into the system you nominated, by EDI, API or QuickBooks. Your desk does not acquire a second place to look.

@graph.name: Is VOS a fair Choco alternative, and is it better than Choco?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both answers turn on the same thing. On order capture the two are worth lining up next to each other, and at getting an accurate order out of a busy kitchen with nobody keying it in we would argue VOS is the better fit, because the customer approves the lines rather than software interpreting a message. On storefronts, sales tooling, CRM and growing the average basket, Choco is doing things VOS has never set out to do, and no table we could draw would change that.

@graph.name: How soon can our accounts start?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors are up and running within 24 to 48 hours, and most of their customers send a first order the same day. There is no IT project, which is often the reason a Choco alternative is on the shortlist at all. Choco does not publish a go-live time, so ask them for one rather than take a number from us.

@graph.name: Can VOS read a photo of a handwritten order?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and that is a real gap against Choco, whose OrderAgent does exactly that. VOS works the other way round: rather than decode what a kitchen already wrote down, it gives them an app that turns speech into an itemized list they confirm. If reading paper matters more to you than that, say so early and we will tell you so.

@graph.name: Does VOS take over from our ERP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Never. VOS works at the intake end and hands the order on, itemized and approved. Everything behind that, picking, invoicing, delivery, runs exactly as it does now in the software you already pay for.

@graph.name: What does VOS cost next to Choco?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are quoted on the distributor side, and their restaurant app is published as free. Choco's own pricing page says it charges a monthly fee based on usage and asks you to talk to sales; we quote per distributor and publish nothing. So the only honest comparison is two quotes, read together.

Very little. Saying what they are short of is not new, and that is the whole interaction. There is no catalog to search and no basket to fill, so the habit lands faster than a storefront usually does.

@graph.name: What about the accounts that will only ever telephone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Let them telephone. Your desk takes those exactly as it does today. Be clear with yourself about one thing though: a call or a voicemail gets no VOS order number, no timestamp and no stock movement. Only what arrives through the app does.

@graph.name: Where do the Choco details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choco's own site, read on 10 October 2026: the module names and descriptions off the homepage and the usage-based line off their pricing page. We have not repeated the growth figures they publish, because those are their numbers and not ours to vouch for. If any of it has moved on since, this page is what needs correcting.
